Subject: Regional quality follow-up and next steps — EU & APAC model suitability

Hi Alice / Pedro,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone has the same context and clear next steps.

Summary of requirements (from your call):
- Primary EU languages: German (de), French (fr), Spanish (es).
- APAC pilot languages: Japanese (ja), Korean (ko) — low-latency edge a plus.
- Hard constraints: false-positive reduction on entity extraction (banking PII) and <1% tolerance for hallucinated regulatory statements.
- Expected monthly volume: ~1.2M generation tokens + ~150k classification/embedding units.
- Security: SOC2 + customer-managed KMS; redact files before transfer.

What Redwood will deliver for the pilot:
1) Shortlist of model variants per region with quantization recommendation and expected token latency.
2) Shared benchmark report (initial run attached) and the prompt set we used to reproduce results.
3) Mutual Action Plan with milestones, evaluation criteria, and success gates.
4) Weekly sync cadence during the 6-week pilot + an ops deep-dive to validate latency SLOs.

Immediate asks from LinguaWave for our team:
- Confirm the five pilot locales and highlight any dialectal priorities (e.g., Swiss German).
- Provide a sample of the critical prompts and a redaction checklist for PII.
- Any internal acceptance thresholds beyond the ones we discussed (we proposed F1 >= 0.88 for NER).

Attachments: EU_benchmark_results_20270618.pdf (topline numbers), APAC_prompt_set_v2.csv, mutual_action_plan_LW.xlsx

Next steps (my side / internal): Marissa will send explicit model recommendations and benchmark links by EOD Wednesday; Soojin will surface APAC latency options; Neha will follow up on procurement timeline and potential early access pricing.

Would you be available for a 30min ops deep-dive next Wednesday (28th) or the following Monday?

Thanks,
Rishi

Hi Alice / Pedro — following Rishi's recap, sharing concrete recommendations and links so you can validate quickly. Long version below; TL;DR at top.

TL;DR — model & config recommendations (pilot):
- EU (de, fr, es): open-llama-70B-qa (16-bit) for generation + distill-finetune for NER; quantize to int8 for cost savings after baseline run. Expected 95th pct token latency: ~180ms on g5.
- JP / KR: opt-japanese-13b (or equivalent with Japanese tokenizer) for generation; use 4-bit quantization and dedicated small-batch routing to keep latency <220ms.
- Fallback: a smaller multilingual 7B model for low-cost burst traffic and as a graceful-degrade path.

Benchmarks & prompt sets:
- Attached PDF contains the EU bench run (EU_benchmark_results_20270618.pdf) — we ran generation & NER evaluation across your sample prompt set. Highlights: German generative QA precision dropped vs en baseline (precision 0.82) on out-of-domain legal snippets.
- Prompt set (APAC_prompt_set_v2.csv) includes masked PII cases and structured-system prompts we recommend.

Quality regression concerns & mitigations:
- Regression risk: cross-lingual hallucination spikes when the model sees mixed-language context and long regulatory clauses. Mitigation: language-identify + prefix-conditioning, and run a lightweight hallucination classifier post-generation (we can deploy as a microservice).
- NER drift monitoring: validate nightly on a stratified sample; if F1 drops >0.04 vs baseline, trigger a canary rollback for that model variant.

Evaluation plan (acceptance criteria):
- NER: F1 >= 0.88 across each EU locale (macro-average).
- Generative correctness: domain-specific fact checks with an automated extraction followed by a rule-based validator; hallucination rate <2% on regulatory prompts.
- Latency: p95 token latency target per locale (EU: <200ms, APAC: <250ms) under pilot traffic profile.

Operational notes:
- We'll provide a reproducible eval harness (link above) and a set of deterministic seeds for prompt runs.
- Data handling: please confirm the redaction checklist; anything not redacted should be treated under the pilot NDA.

Attachments included again: EU_benchmark_results_20270618.pdf, APAC_prompt_set_v2.csv, mutual_action_plan_LW.xlsx

Action items assigned:
- LinguaWave: upload one redacted + one semi-redacted sample per locale into the Drive (Alice).
- Redwood (Marissa): run a focused German legal snippet re-benchmark with additional context-window reductions and share numbers by Thu EOD.
- Redwood (Soojin): propose APAC hardware routing options and latency tradeoffs by Thu.
- Neha: draft pilot commercial terms and a proposed start date window (Jul 5–12).

We'll use the Drive folder linked by Rishi for all artifacts. Happy to jump on the Wed 28th ops deep-dive at 09:00 BST.

Thanks,
Marissa
